business: Methea (a research-methodology navigator for Master's and PhD students)
target: Master's and PhD students in social sciences, education, business and communication, writing a proposal or thesis with a qualitative component
where: Online; students at English-speaking universities (UK, US, EU, Australia)

segments.name: International Master's student on scholarship or loan
Working professional doing a part-time Master's, MBA or DBA

behaviours.name: Deadline panic buyer
behaviours.how: Ignores tools for months, then pays for anything that helps the night before a supervisor meeting.

behaviours.name: Free-tier maximiser
behaviours.how: Uses the free version of everything and only pays when hard-blocked.

behaviours.name: Already pays for ChatGPT
behaviours.how: Has ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro and tries to do everything in it first.

behaviours.name: Integrity-cautious
behaviours.how: Worried about AI policies; checks whether a tool is allowed before using it.

behaviours.name: Follows peers
behaviours.how: Uses what classmates in the cohort WhatsApp group recommend.

behaviours.name: Methods-confident
behaviours.how: Feels they already understand methodology and only want a quick check.

objections: ChatGPT already does this and I already pay for it
Will my university treat this as AI misuse?
My supervisor is supposed to help with this for free
$49 is a lot on a student budget
I only need help with one part, not the whole chain
Will the theories and citations actually be accurate?
Does this work for my discipline or a mixed-methods design?
habits: your research proposal is due in three weeks
you meet your supervisor for 30 minutes once a month
you work 20 hours a week alongside your studies
you are writing in your second language
your cohort shares tools in a WhatsApp group
